title: Service Catalog

sections.heading: Key concepts
sections.content: The Service Catalog presents users with Catalog Items organized into categories. A Catalog Item can have Variables (input fields) and Variable Sets (groups of reusable variables). An order generates a Requested Item (RITM), which is itself attached to a Request (REQ).

sections.heading: Types of items
sections.content: A Record Producer creates a record directly in another table (e.g. an incident) from a catalog form, without going through the standard RITM process. An Order Guide lets you order several related Catalog Items at once.

sections.heading: Automation
sections.content: Submitting a Catalog Item triggers an associated Workflow (or Flow Designer flow), which can include approval steps (sysapproval_approver) and tasks (Catalog Task). Catalog Client Scripts control variable behavior (visibility, default values) and can be marked 'Isolate script' to run in an isolated environment.

pieges: Confusing a Record Producer with a standard Catalog Item: a Record Producer does not create a RITM, it creates the target record directly.
Forgetting that an Order Guide is used to group several items, not to configure a single one in more detail.
Thinking the Workflow/Flow triggers when the item is added to the cart rather than when the order is submitted (checkout).
